about: CLAIMS-1b W1: four buyer walks of the served page. Each buyer read https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/bot-team-kit/ cold, as GitHub Pages served it at the commit below, in a browser: every control clicked (write, paste a secret, claim done, load the traced run, clear, every cost-case box, including emptied and non-numeric ones), every explainer and number read, every link opened. A gap is something the buyer needed that the page did not answer; each is fixed on the page or marked as needing a decision only the owner can make. What a buyer checked and found already answered is kept beside the gaps. The page reads this file to show the walks. Round 2: the same four buyers read the page again, cold, as served at round 2's commit (after round 1's fixes), with the seal and the code open beside it; round 1's record is kept as it was, and walks with no round are round 1. Round 3 (CLAIMS-1c W2): the same four buyers read the page again, cold, as served at round 3's commit (after the page's own modules were mutation-gated), with every receipt open beside it; each walk lists what was checked.
walker: Kar (Claude Opus 5.5), one buyer at a time

walks.focus: what it costs, what it saves, where every figure comes from

gaps.asked: What does it cost us to get this deployed and supported?
gaps.gap: the page said support is agreed per deployment, but not whether help is charged or how it is agreed
gaps.change: Help is scoped in writing: the scope and fee of any roll-out help or support are written into the deployment's agreement before any work.

gaps.asked: And what will that fee be?
gaps.gap: no fee is stated; by the estate's standing rule no price of ours goes on a product page
gaps.decision: Simon sets the scope and fee of roll-out help and support for each deployment, in its agreement; it stays off the page.

gaps.asked: Where does the starting number of hours come from?
gaps.gap: the boxes start at values the page did not explain
gaps.change: The page says the boxes start at the cost-case kernel's own defaults, not at a measurement of your team.

gaps.asked: How would we know the share of the work it takes off?
gaps.gap: the share was marked as an estimate with no way to firm it up
gaps.change: The share box now says: run it on one team for a fortnight and compare the hours.

gaps.asked: When were the outside prices read, and is VAT in or out?
gaps.gap: the sources list named each source but not when it was read, nor the currency basis
gaps.change: Each source now shows the date it was read, from the sourced basis itself, and the list ends with the currency basis (GBP, ex-VAT).

alreadyAnswered: an emptied box asks for every box to be filled; a zero saving is said plainly, never shown as a negative
the electricity line is explained as an always-on laptop's extra draw, more than the kit needs
the rented-assistant route keeps the staff time; the cloud route takes the same share off and sends every line out
no licence fee (MIT), no meter, no AI service called

walks.focus: where data goes, what is redacted, what could be tampered with

gaps.asked: Does the try-it panel send what I type anywhere?
gaps.gap: the panel did not say
gaps.change: Start here now says nothing you type leaves your browser: the page can only fetch its own files.

gaps.asked: Can the page itself load or send anything else?
gaps.gap: the page had no content security policy
gaps.change: The page now carries a content security policy: scripts, fetches and styles from its own origin only, no objects, no forms, no base changes.

gaps.asked: Which secret shapes, exactly?
gaps.gap: the page pointed at the sealed battery without naming the shapes
gaps.change: Security now lists every shape the fix was measured on, read from the sealed battery.

gaps.asked: Is the file really append-only? Could someone edit it?
gaps.gap: the white paper called the file append-only, which the kit does not enforce
gaps.change: The white paper now says the kit only ever appends to the file, and a new risk answer says to protect it with file permissions, and to use the signed team feed for tamper evidence.

gaps.asked: Who can read the feed?
gaps.gap: the roll-out did not say who should have access
gaps.change: Roll-out step one now says: readable only by the bots' account and whoever audits them.

gaps.asked: What if two bots write at the same moment?
gaps.gap: not answered
gaps.change: A risk answer: each line goes to disk in one append call, and any line that comes back unreadable is counted and reported, never dropped.

gaps.asked: Our bots run on more than one machine.
gaps.gap: not answered
gaps.change: A risk answer: one feed per machine, each with its own morning page; merging signed feeds from several machines is what the team feed in ai-first-company does.

gaps.asked: How long does a roll-out take, and who does it?
gaps.gap: no timetable or staffing is stated, and none can be typed in without a deployment to measure

walks.focus: every claim on the page against the seal and the code

gaps.asked: The badge says the sealed claims held. CLAIMS-1b seals more claims than the table shows: where are E1, G0, G1, G2, C1, T1, P1 and W1?
gaps.gap: the page showed only the claims measured in receipts/step1b.json; the rest of the seal had no verdict on the page
gaps.change: receipts/claims.json, written by tools/claims.mjs and re-derived on GitHub's runner, carries the verdict of every claim the seal names, against the seal's own bar; the badge and the claims table read it.

gaps.asked: 'Cannot leak a secret', 'secrets never reach disk' — even a shape it has no rule for?
gaps.gap: the opening, the adoption card and the security card promised every secret, while the risks answer says an unknown shape is stored as written
gaps.change: Each of those lines now says the secret shapes the kit has rules for, and the security card points to the measured list.

gaps.asked: 'It cannot stop the flag' — can a bot not attach a made-up hash?
gaps.gap: it can: the flag checks that proof is shaped like proof, not that it is true
gaps.change: The answer now says a bot escapes the flag only by attaching something shaped like proof, and that is exactly what the auditor re-runs.

gaps.asked: Where does this sit under UK GDPR?
gaps.gap: the page said less personal data by design, but not who is the controller, whether anyone else processes the data, or how retention and erasure work
gaps.change: A data-protection answer: the kit runs on your machine and sends nothing, so it adds no outside processor and no transfer abroad; you are the controller of what the feed holds; emails and card numbers are removed as a line is written; retention and erasure are operations on your own file, and the next morning page is rebuilt without a removed line.

gaps.asked: Does this page itself set cookies or track me?
gaps.gap: the page did not say
gaps.change: The security card now says the page sets no cookies, stores nothing in the browser and loads no analytics or outside script; its content security policy lets it load only its own files.

gaps.asked: Our engineer ran npm test and got one suite out of six.
gaps.gap: package.json's test script ran only the first build's suite, and npm run check ran none of the receipt checks
gaps.change: npm test now runs every suite and npm run check runs the whole proof list CI runs apart from witness; Start here names it.
